newsitem.title: UK: Texaco says Atlantic oil test starts after protest.
newsitem.headline: Texaco says Atlantic oil test starts after protest.

text.p: U.S. major Texaco Inc began oil exploration seismic tests in the north Atlantic on Monday evening after Greenpeace ended a protest using inflatable boats, the company said on Tuesday.
"They are shooting seismic now...Greenpeace are nowhere to be seen," a Texaco spokesman said.

He said the tests by oil exploration vessel Pacific Horizon began late on Monday evening, continued overnight and were still going on at mid-morning in seas 180 nautical miles (330 km) east of the tiny barren Atlantic island of Rockall off Scotland.

Ten Greenpeace activists sailed three inflatable boats close to the Pacific Horizon on Monday, the company said, delaying the start of the tests in tranche 36, block 153 of Britain's 17th offshore licensing round.
Permits under the round have been awarded mainly in the Rockall Trough sea area.

The Texaco spokesman said the exploration ship had delayed its start due to safety concerns because the activists on Monday had in effect threatened to throw themselves into the water in front of the vessel to prevent it starting work.
The ship MV Greenpeace, which had launched the inflatables, withdrew from the area later on Monday, Texaco said.
Greenpeace called the tests illegal, saying the British government had failed to ensure a full environmental impact assessment had been made.
The protest was part of a Greenpeace campaign against plans to open up Atlantic waters for oil exploration.
Greeenpeace is seeking to take the British government to court this week over Atlantic oil exploration plans.
